arc: hook (cold DM sent) → problem ×5 (hundred reach-outs, rude reply, lists, not interested, volume) → turn + mark reveal → feature ×7 (detects, engages, website, target, monitors, intent signals, prioritize) → workflow (campaigns) → benefit ×3 (no cold prospects, 3-5x more, autopilot) → cta + logo

scenes.title: LinkedIn DM typed and sent, button floods the frame
scenes.summary: On a soft breathing tile grid, "Mmh..." types at the top while a wireframe LinkedIn browser window springs up from the bottom. The window blurs away as its message composer zooms out to centre, the cold message ("Dear Ethan Carter, I'm about to send you a LinkedIn message you didn't ask for...") typing fast inside it. A cursor sweeps in, clicks the blue Send button (it flips to "Sent"), and a blue disc grows out of the button to flood the whole frame as the card lifts off with motion blur.
scenes.build: BrowserWindow (skeleton LinkedIn layout) and DmCard (composer with a chars prop for typing) are positioned so the card first sits inside the window at WIN_DM_SCALE, then its left/top/scale are lerped to centre by one zoom value. The cursor follows a measured per-frame TRAVEL_P table and the Cursor component derives lean and ghost trails from vx/vy; the flood is a circle div whose radius interpolates 0→2400 from the Send button centre.
scenes.reuse: Borrow for any 'the old way' cold open built from a UI action: type into a composer, click, flood the frame with the button colour as a hard cut into the next scene. Swap the message text, avatar and button colour. Don't copy the LinkedIn chrome or Ethan Carter persona as-is.

scenes.title: "Sent" on a blue flood
scenes.summary: One second on the full LinkedIn-blue flood left by scene 01: the word "Sent" fades up white in the centre while the click cursor fades out. In the last frames the blue thins to a tint as the field of sent DM cards arrives underneath.
scenes.build: A blue overlay div whose opacity drops 1→0.42 at the end, over CardField rendered at t = frame - 30 so the field is already mid-pull-back. The real work (parallax field of MiniCards and cursors) is in components/CardField.tsx, shared with scene 03.
scenes.reuse: Only useful as the handoff between a flood cut and the card-field scene; take CardField instead.

scenes.title: Camera pulls back through a field of sent DMs
scenes.summary: Nine small 'sent DM' cards and five cursors are scattered at different depths; the camera pulls back through them (near cards move more and are blurred, far ones small) while the last of the blue tint clears. "After a hundred reach-outs today..." swings in from the left in 3D, word by word, the field fades, the line centres, and "maybe someone will respond" types below in link blue.
scenes.build: CardField(t) gives each card a depth d and computes k = (S-1)/d + 1 from one pull-back scale S, so parallax and depth blur come from one number. HundredLines(t) holds both TypeLine rows with a rotateY/translate3d swing-in; it is shared with scene 04 so the cut is invisible. This file only stacks GridBackground, CardField, a tint and HundredLines.
scenes.reuse: Use the CardField parallax idea for 'you did this a hundred times' or volume problem beats; swap MiniCard for any repeated UI card. Copy CardField.tsx and HundredLines.tsx with it, since the scene file alone holds no visuals.

scenes.title: Notification click opens the rude reply thread
scenes.summary: The LinkedIn window rises again under the fading lines from 03 and "Ohhh!" types at the top. A blue minimised message bar with a pulsing red badge sits bottom-right; the cursor lands on it, the camera pushes in 2.3x, click. The thread card grows out of the bar, swings to centre and zooms to 2.2x so we read the reply up close ("F*CK YOU / Best regards" under the original DM), then pulls back as "Let's be honest" types below and everything blurs up and away.
scenes.build: A 'stage' div holds the window and bar under one translate+scale camera computed from Z/tx/ty, with a toScreen() helper so the cursor is placed in stage coordinates. ReplyCard is clip-path revealed from the bar height (inset top) while bottom-anchored, then blended into centre-anchored keyframes for the read-close and pull-back, with a short blur spike on the zoom-out. Uses BrowserWindow, ReplyCard, HundredLines (continued at t = frame + 102), TypeLine and Cursor.
scenes.reuse: Strong pattern for 'click a notification, the message expands, read the punchline up close': swap the reply copy, the avatar and the bar colour. Keep the clip-path grow-from-bar and the push-in/read/pull-back camera. Don't reuse the profanity or LinkedIn styling for other brands.

scenes.title: "Your problem isn't what you sell" text card
scenes.summary: On the drifting tile grid, "Your problem isn't what you sell" falls in word by word at centre (each word resolves out of blur with a small rise, "what you sell" in link blue), floats for a beat, then drifts up into a blur.
scenes.build: A single TypeLine (word units every 3 frames, float, exitAt 60) over GridBackground with a slow drift. All the motion lives in components/TypeLine.tsx.
scenes.reuse: A one-line statement card; reach for TypeLine itself rather than this file.

scenes.title: Spreadsheet rises under "hours building lists"
scenes.summary: A green-headed spreadsheet (skeleton cells, column letters A-J, 22 rows) rises from the bottom on a plane tilted back and rotated -5 degrees, drifts up slowly, then drops back out. Above it, along the same -5 degree slant, "It's spending hours building lists" types word by word with "building lists" in spreadsheet green.
scenes.build: Sheet component (pure divs, random(seed) cell widths) inside a perspective(2400px) rotateX(16deg) rotate(-5deg) wrapper; its top is rise + drift + drop from three interpolates. The headline is a TypeLine in a rotated container that drifts at 0.6x the sheet.
scenes.reuse: Use for 'manual busywork' pain points: swap Sheet for any tool screenshot or mock (CRM, inbox) and recolour the emphasis word to the tool's colour.

scenes.title: Three rude replies fan up on a tilted plane
scenes.summary: Three wide reply cards rise one after another (4-frame stagger) onto a plane tilted back 22 degrees, each with an avatar and a curt reply: "Go to hell. / Kind regards", "I couldn't care less. / Sincerely", "Do whatever you want. / Best wishes". "contacting people who are not interested" types along the bottom with "not interested" in blue; at the end the cards blur and the line shrinks away.
scenes.build: A perspective container with three RudeReply cards, each rotateX(22deg) plus a small z-rotation, sliding up 420px with outCubic and a slow sine drift. TypeLine for the caption; exit is a shared blur/scale over the last 6 frames.
scenes.reuse: Good for showing negative feedback, bad reviews or failed outcomes as a stack of UI cards. Swap the lines tuple and avatars; keep the stagger and tilt.

scenes.title: Wall of message threads at three depths
scenes.summary: Fifteen message-thread cards fill the frame at different depths: near ones large and soft, far ones small and washed toward white, all drifting while the camera creeps in 5%. "and hoping volume will fix the problem" types at centre ("fix the problem" in blue) and the whole picture fades to white.
scenes.build: A WALL array of {x, y, d}; each ReplyCard is placed with k = (S-1)/d + 1 parallax from one creep scale S, scale 0.55/d, blur when d < 0.9 or > 1.45, a white 'wash' via opacity for far cards, and zIndex from depth.
scenes.reuse: Reuse for 'too much of X' (emails, tickets, notifications): swap ReplyCard for your card and keep the depth/blur/wash rules. Similar parallax idea to CardField in scene 03, but static and denser.

scenes.title: "It's time to change" slam-zoom into a burst and logo
scenes.summary: "It's time to change" types with "change" letter by letter in an orange gradient while a pink radial bloom rises behind it. The camera slams into the word "to" (9x zoom with blur), a white flash and a ring of orange dashes burst at centre, the strawberry mark pops in spinning from -140 degrees, slides left, and the wordmark "strawberry" tracks in beside it with letter-spacing tightening from 0.32em.
scenes.build: TypeLine inside a full-frame div scaled 1→9 with transformOrigin pinned on "to" and a matching blur ramp; GridBackground bloom prop fades in the pink. ParticleRing draws ~44 elongated dashes around a point that grow, spin and thin out over 34 frames; the mark uses outBack scale + rotation, the wordmark per-letter blur-in plus an animated letterSpacing.
scenes.reuse: A ready problem→solution pivot with a logo reveal: swap the line, the mark image and WORD. The zoom-through-a-word into a particle burst works for any 'turn' beat. Note the code's wordmark reads "strawberry", not the template's product name.

scenes.title: Radar rings pop up prospect avatars
scenes.summary: Salmon concentric rings radiate from the mark in a white disc at the bottom centre, breathing gently. Six round prospect avatars pop up across the rings one after another (outBack), bobbing. "detects high-intent people in your market" types above, "in your market" in orange gradient. On the way out everything fades except one avatar, who drifts right and gains his own small ring for scene 11.
scenes.build: Radar component: stacked filled circles that grow in staggered order and pulse 2% on a sine. Avatars are absolutely placed Img discs with staggered outBack scale; the chosen one is lerped to ETHAN_END and redrawn above a second, lighter Radar.
scenes.reuse: Use for 'finds / detects / matches people' features (recruiting, sales, dating): swap avatars and the centre logo. The one-avatar-survives exit is a neat handoff into a single-user story.

scenes.title: Prospect wired to Invitation and Message step cards
scenes.summary: One prospect avatar sits inside a small pink ring on the right. Two step cards pop in on the left ("Send Invitation, Step 1" and "Send Message, Step 2", blue headers with icon discs) and a dashed connector draws from the first card to the avatar. "engages them at the right moment with" types above, then "personalized LinkedIn outreach" in orange; everything slides out left with blur.
scenes.build: StepCard (lucide UserPlus/Send icons, skeleton body) with outBack scale; the connector is an SVG path with strokeDasharray and a dashoffset animated via pathLength. Radar provides the ring around the avatar.
scenes.reuse: Use when a product takes automated steps toward one person or object: swap the StepCard titles/icons and the avatar. The animated dashed connector is the reusable bit.

scenes.title: Website URL typed, Next Step clicked, AI fills the form
scenes.summary: A wide white form card slides in from the right while "You enter your website" types above. "yourcompany.com" types into the Website field next to a red Analyze button, a cursor rises from the bottom and clicks the orange gradient "Next Step" button (small orange particle burst). The card grows and Company Name, Industry and Company Description rows appear with loading-bar skeletons, while the headline becomes "Our AI understands your market", then deletes "market" and retypes "offer". The card drops away at the end.
scenes.build: Pure-div form with frame-driven character slicing for the URL and a blinking caret; card height/top interpolate after the click; Skeleton bars fill with a gradient. The headline swap is two stacked lines: TypeLine for the stem and a hand-sliced span that types, backspaces and retypes the last word. Uses Cursor (press + ring) and ParticleRing.
scenes.reuse: A compact 'step 1: paste your URL, the AI does the rest' onboarding demo. Swap field labels, URL and the word-swap pair (market/offer). Keep the type-backspace-retype trick for any headline that should change one word.

scenes.title: Lead cards pop around the mark on dashed connectors
scenes.summary: An orange burst leaves the mark in a white extruded disc at centre; three lead cards pop up around it on a plane tilted about -8 degrees, joined by dashed connectors: Jasper Krog (CMO), Petra Sievinen (Head of Paid Acquisition), Julie Sockeel (Creative Strategist). "and clearly defines who you should target" types above with "target" letter by letter in orange. The cards scatter outward with blur at the end.
scenes.build: Lead cards are white divs over an offset tinted 'extruded base' div for a chunky 3D look; dashed SVG paths are revealed with an animated clip-path inset. The whole group sits in one rotate(tilt) wrapper; ParticleRing at t = frame gives the opening burst.
scenes.reuse: Use for ICP / audience / persona features: swap names, roles and avatars. The extruded-card trick (second div offset 14px below) is a cheap depth effect worth borrowing.

scenes.title: Tilted analytics dashboard with AI Agent card
scenes.summary: A huge analytics panel rises from the bottom on a steep isometric-style tilt: five stat tiles (6, 582, 235, 98, $782) slide up, then three colored wave lines (teal, purple, pink) draw themselves across it. A white "AI Agent · Active" card with a bot icon, green status dot and pulsing orange dots hovers above the panel. "It then monitors buying signals in real time" types above, "in real time" in orange.
scenes.build: Panel and agent card share transform rotateX(42deg) rotateZ(-12deg) inside a perspective container; wavePath() builds smooth cubic paths from seeded samples and draws them with pathLength=1 and strokeDashoffset. The agent card hovers on a sine and enters with outBack scale.
scenes.reuse: Strong generic 'AI is watching your data' shot: swap stat values, line colours and the agent label. The tilted-panel-rising-from-below framing works for any dashboard screenshot too.

scenes.title: Three intent-signal polaroid cards push in
scenes.summary: "to spot actions that indicate intent like" types at centre and floats, then blurs out. Three polaroid-style cards with big line icons arrive one at a time from the right, each pushing the earlier ones left: "job changes" (briefcase), "competitor interactions" (message bubble), "meaningful engagement" (megaphone). Each is tilted, bobs, and has a pulsing coral dot at its corner.
scenes.build: Each card has three stops [[x,y]...] and two global shift progresses (s1, s2) at frames 96 and 144; position = a + (b-a)*s1 + (d-b)*s2, so one card arriving shifts the others. Icons are lucide Briefcase / MessageCircle / Megaphone.
scenes.reuse: Use for any 'three kinds of X' list beat; swap labels and icons. The stop/shift pattern scales to more cards.

scenes.title: Prospect table scored with a fire sweep
scenes.summary: A tilted prospects table rises (navy sidebar, eight rows like "Julien Moreau, Head of Communications, Publicis" with 1-3 fire emoji scores) while "AI agents score and prioritize the most" types above. As "active prospects" follows in orange, a sweep of flickering fire emoji with an orange glow crosses the top rows, which then glow peach. The table blurs away and the purple "Send Invitation, Step 1" card resolves in its place as a handoff to scene 17.
scenes.build: Table is a 2300px div with rotateX(40deg) rotateZ(-9deg) in a perspective container; rows stagger in. The fire sweep is 18 seeded emoji spans with sin-driven flicker plus a blurred radial gradient, translated across by one interpolate; 'hot' rows lerp background and shadow colour. StepCard is the handoff element.
scenes.reuse: Use for lead scoring, ranking or 'AI picks the best' moments: swap rows and the sweep glyph. The emoji fire sweep + row glow is a playful highlight device. The final StepCard handoff belongs to this template's flow; drop it when used alone.

scenes.title: Campaign step cards on a dashed rail, camera pans
scenes.summary: On a white dot grid, five campaign step cards appear left to right on a dashed rail, all on a plane tilted back and yawed left: Send Invitation (purple, "97 contact(s)" / "9 answer(s)"), Send Message with "AI Personalized Message", then message previews like "{FirstName}, we booked 12 demos in 5 days using...". "automatically create and launch" types above; the camera pans left along the rail with motion blur and "personalized outreach campaigns" types further down the world.
scenes.build: One 'campaign-world' div with rotateX/rotateY (settling from a stronger tilt) and translateX(pan) inside a perspective container; the dot grid pans at half speed for parallax. Copy is placed inside the world so it pans with the cards; pan blur is a keyed interpolate.
scenes.reuse: Good for sequences/pipelines/automations: swap step titles, colours, chips and message copy. Keep the in-world copy and half-speed background for a cheap tracking shot.

scenes.title: Sinking red wave under "cold prospects" pill
scenes.summary: A coral area wave (a falling chart line) sweeps in from the left and slowly sinks while "You stop wasting time on" types at centre. A red-orange "cold prospects" pill pops onto the end of the line, then the whole line drifts left out of frame.
scenes.build: wave() builds an SVG area path from two sines plus a downward slope, shifted per frame; the svg's left and top are interpolated for the sweep and sink. The pill is a div with outBack scale next to a TypeLine.
scenes.reuse: Use for 'stop doing X' benefits: swap the pill word. The sinking wave reads as decline without needing a real chart.

scenes.title: "3-5x more" slams in, then replies and demos pills
scenes.summary: Orange speed streaks race across the top and bottom as a giant gradient "3-5x more" (330px) slams in from the right with motion blur, pans left to reveal "more", then zooms past the lens. A coral "replies" pill pops with fire-emoji wings, "and", then a "demos" pill bursts out of an orange particle ring, over a drifting field of blurred replies/demos pills at depth.
scenes.build: One huge gradient-clipped text div moved by slide + pan and scaled 1→3.2 with a keyed motion-blur interpolate; streaks are seeded divs wrapping across the width. Background pills use the same depth/parallax/blur rule as the card fields; ParticleRing for the demos burst.
scenes.reuse: Use for a headline multiplier stat ("10x faster", "3-5x more"): swap the number and the two outcome pills. The pan-to-reveal-then-zoom-past is the borrowable move.

scenes.title: "all of this on autopilot" pill and road
scenes.summary: "all of this on" types at centre, a coral "autopilot" pill pops beside it and the line lifts, then a pink perspective road (a trapezoid with red edges) draws up from the bottom toward the pill before everything blurs out.
scenes.build: TypeLine plus outBack pill (same treatment as scene 18); the road is an SVG trapezoid whose apex height and widths interpolate with one progress value.
scenes.reuse: Near-duplicate of scene 18's line-plus-pill; the growing road trapezoid is the only extra idea.

scenes.title: Tagline, logo lockup and a clicked "Try now" button
scenes.summary: "Reach buyers when they are ready" types at centre ("ready" in orange) as the background warms with a peach wash. The strawberry mark drops in above, slides left as the wordmark "strawberry" tracks in at 92px, and a coral "Try now" pill pops below, its label typing in. A cursor glides up from the bottom, clicks the button (press + ring + orange particle burst) and rests there to the final frame.
scenes.build: GridBackground with bloom and warm props plus an extra diagonal gradient; mark outBack drop, wordmark per-letter blur with animated letterSpacing (same lockup as scene 09). Cursor, ParticleRing and a press-scaled button complete the click. Nothing exits.
scenes.reuse: A complete end card: swap the tagline, mark, WORD and button label. Keep the cursor-clicks-CTA ending; it reads as 'go do it'. The wordmark in code is "strawberry".
